entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Osorkon I was an ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the 22nd Dynasty, ruling from approximately 912 to 888 BCE. His territory extended across much of the Levant, including modern-day Israel and Palestine.

As a major figure in this period, Osorkon's reign is notable for its complex diplomatic relationships with neighboring powers, particularly the Assyrians. He formed alliances with the Phoenicians and other local leaders to resist Assyrian expansion, while also maintaining a strong Egyptian presence in the region.

Osorkon's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he played a significant role in shaping the cultural and political landscape of the ancient Near East. His successors would go on to play important roles in the development of the Persian Empire and the rise of Judaism.

The sheer breadth of Osorkon's influence is perhaps best captured by a single, striking statistic: his reign saw the construction of over 30 major temples across Egypt and the Levant, a testament to his commitment to the gods and the enduring legacy of ancient Egyptian culture.
